evals.setup: A small Python repo with pytest and a git history of about 40 commits. src/billing/invoice.py changed in 12 commits, 3 with 'fix:' subjects that touched no test, and no test imports it. tests/test_orders.py mocks src/orders/repo.py (an owned module) and asserts save() call order; 4 'refactor:' commits changed it. tests/test_cart.py and tests/test_checkout.py both assert the same cart total. One test calls time.sleep(3). There is no coverage config and no CI.
expected_behavior: Times the full suite and a single test file and records both commands in a Vitals table
Runs scripts/test-history.py drift, fixes and refactors rather than hand-rolling git log pipelines
Files a blind-spot candidate for src/billing/invoice.py that names a seam with what it catches and misses, and cites the untested fix commits by SHA
Files a waste candidate for tests/test_orders.py that names the prune-tests category (tied to the implementation) and what still guards the behaviour
Reports the duplicated cart-total assertion and the sleep as waste with a cost
Does not add coverage tooling to the project
Writes docs/test-review/<date>-<slug>/README.md plus one card per candidate, adds the review to docs/test-review/README.md, and stops after opening the report PR without implementing anything

evals.setup: A TypeScript repo with vitest. A scan has just been confirmed by the user with batch C1 (blind spot at parsePrice(input), behaviours: rejects negative amounts, rounds to cents) and C2 (waste: three tests in src/__tests__/format.test.ts asserting a private helper). parsePrice currently accepts negative amounts.
expected_behavior: Calls the Skill tool with tdd for C1 and does not ask the user to confirm the seam again
For the rounding behaviour, which already passes, breaks the code temporarily to see the new test fail, reverts, and names the mutation in the commit body
Treats the negative-amount test failing against unchanged code as a live defect: keeps the test, fixes parsePrice in the same PR, and marks the row as a live defect
Calls the Skill tool with prune-tests for C2 and times the affected tests before and after
Opens one PR per candidate, C2's based on C1's branch, and never merges
Updates the status table with each PR and ends with a loose-ends audit before reporting

evals.setup: A Python repo where src/payments/gateway.py builds its HTTP client inside charge() with no way to inject it, and the only tests patch gateway._build_client and gateway._sign. The suite runs on pre-commit via lefthook and takes 45 seconds.
expected_behavior: Lists gateway.py under Hand-offs with a /arch-review src/payments line instead of filing a blind-spot candidate that mocks internals
Files an infra candidate to move the 45-second suite from pre-commit to pre-push, routed through setup-lefthook
Marks the tests patching private functions as waste tied to the implementation, with a rewrite rather than delete action when they are the only guard of charging behaviour
Keeps the scan scoped to src/payments and says so in the report header
